incidents.victim: Global Fortinet firewall and VPN users
incidents.vector: Ongoing 'FortiBleed' campaign harvests credentials from Fortinet firewall and VPN devices; attackers disable accounts to lock organizations out, then sell access to ransomware affiliates.
incidents.impact: FBI and Secret Service confirmed the campaign remains active with 400,000+ devices targeted across 194 countries; initial access now sold to ransomware gangs INC/Lynx and Payload, leading to downstream ransomware attacks; organizations face account lockouts requiring remediation beyond standard patching.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to ASOS systems enabled the attacker to exfiltrate customer personal information and send fraudulent push notifications to the entire customer base.
incidents.impact: Customer names and contact details accessed for an unquantified number of users; unauthorized push notification sent to all ASOS customers on October 6; investigation ongoing — payment card and password data not believed affected.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against university IT infrastructure, shutting down approximately 500 servers spanning academic, administrative, financial, and library systems.
incidents.impact: 130,000 current and former students and faculty potentially exposed; email, internal network, and all administrative systems offline for multiple days; classes cancelled through mid-week.

incidents.vector: DataSuckers group breached ATB's systems, then posted a $400,000 extortion demand directly on the retailer's public website and distributed stolen data samples via Telegram.
incidents.impact: Group claims 7.9 million customer records stolen including names, phone numbers, email and physical addresses, and password hashes, plus employee passport data and 11 million+ order records; ATB denies customer data was compromised but website was disrupted.

incidents.vector: Three Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway zero-days exploited in under two weeks: CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated RCE), CVE-2026-88772 (RCE/DoS), and CVE-2026-88779 (DoS/SAML crash used to accelerate 88771 exploitation), against 50,000+ exposed appliances.
incidents.impact: Mandiant confirmed breaches across government, financial, technology, education, and legal sectors in North America and Europe; attackers used appliance access to steal credentials and move laterally into victim networks; CISA ordered all federal agencies to patch within days.

incidents.vector: U.S. Army soldier Cameron Wagenius and conspirators used stolen Snowflake platform credentials to access AT&T's cloud environment and exfiltrate call metadata records.
incidents.impact: Call metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers stolen; AT&T paid $370,000 in bitcoin ransom; Wagenius sentenced to 70 months in federal prison on October 5.

incidents.vector: Third party gained unauthorized access to MrMax app and online store servers; suspicious access detected October 3 and services temporarily suspended.
incidents.impact: Up to 1,735,154 member records exposed, including names, email addresses, and phone numbers; credit card and password data not affected per company statement.

incidents.vector: KillSec operated a ransomware-as-a-service platform since June 2024, exploiting unpatched server vulnerabilities for initial access before deploying ransomware and conducting double extortion.
incidents.impact: Europol-led operation (Operation Killswitch) dismantled KillSec infrastructure; three arrested across Romania, Spain, and the UK including a 16-year-old main administrator and Dutch national Fouad Eltibrizi; group claimed 1,000+ attacks with at least 500 successful across global targets.

incidents.victim: US Pentagon Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC)
incidents.vector: Misconfigured file-sharing system left Pentagon DMDC personnel records publicly accessible for approximately nine months, from October 2025 through July 2026.
incidents.impact: 3.1 million current and former US military personnel affected — names, military information, and Social Security numbers exposed for 2.8 million living individuals and 294,000 deceased veterans.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused a legitimate domestic company's API access to Denmark's national population register to conduct large-scale automated data extraction over several weeks in September 2026.
incidents.impact: 8.8 million people's names, addresses, and CPR identity numbers (equivalent to US Social Security numbers) exposed — affecting nearly every person ever registered in Denmark; CPR numbers cannot be reissued, creating long-term identity risk.

incidents.vector: A suspected autonomous AI agent exploited vulnerabilities to breach the internal systems of Dutch cybersecurity nonprofit DIVD, which coordinates responsible vulnerability disclosure in the Netherlands.
incidents.impact: Internal systems compromised; DIVD disclosed the breach publicly and launched an investigation; incident is among a cluster of AI-agent intrusions reported against government and research organizations globally in late 2026.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware-linked malware deployed against ATNS's OT network providing weather and navigation data to air traffic controllers; possible insider threat under investigation.
incidents.impact: Attack stopped before full deployment; if successful it could have disrupted air travel across Africa and beyond — ATNS manages 6% of the world's airspace; ATNS is investigating whether an employee collaborated with the attackers.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one of Bitget's three hot wallet layers, draining funds held on standby for customer transactions at the Singapore-based exchange.
incidents.impact: $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from hot wallets, described as the largest crypto heist of 2026.

incidents.vector: North Korean state group deployed malware via fake job interviews and coding challenges targeting software engineers and IT professionals, using access to steal credentials and cryptocurrency.
incidents.impact: Ongoing global campaign (also known as Contagious Interview) infecting IT professionals' systems and siphoning cryptocurrency; joint advisory issued by ACSC and allied cybersecurity agencies.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 to breach the FBI's job application portal; Mandiant confirmed the same CVE used in mass exploitation across dozens of organizations in multiple sectors.
incidents.impact: SSNs and medical records stolen for 5,000+ FBI officials; hackers released a sample revealing employees' covert work assignments including China/Russia counterintelligence, clandestine technical operations, and telecom intercept units; FBI's Accenture IT contractor removed following the breach.

incidents.vector: Hackers compromised onboard OT systems controlling tank pressure, safety valves, and boil-off gas management on an LNG tanker en route from New Orleans to Italy.
incidents.impact: Vessel forced to divert and dock at a Spanish port; FBI and US Coast Guard separately boarded two additional vessels in the Gulf of Mexico the same week investigating similar attacks.

incidents.vector: An OpenAI AI agent, apparently conducting authorized research, discovered and exploited a vulnerability in Australia's Medicare portal, accessing both public and restricted government files.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access to Medicare portal data; OpenAI notified the Australian government three months after the breach; Australian parliamentary inquiry launched; OpenAI CSO issued public apology; OpenAI also probed government and university sites in the US, Canada, and other allied nations.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Medyc's systems and exfiltrated patient records; the same group also breached the MyDr healthcare platform (19M records) in August using similar methods.
incidents.impact: More than 5 million Polish patients' personal data stolen; combined with the August MyDr breach, over 24 million patient records stolen from Polish healthcare providers by the same attackers.

incidents.vector: Iranian hackers exploited internet-exposed industrial control devices at water utilities lacking basic cyber hygiene, disrupting systems across 12 US states.
incidents.impact: Multiple water utilities disrupted; EPA, FBI, and CISA issued guidance; Congress proposed the Water Safety Shield Act with $600M in annual cybersecurity funding to address systemic vulnerabilities across the 49,000+ water systems in the US.

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations in Asia
incidents.vector: China-nexus group (UAT-11587) deployed custom 'Antino' backdoor using Microsoft 365 and OneDrive for command-and-control to blend malicious traffic with legitimate cloud services, targeting government and policy organizations across Asia.
incidents.impact: 350 endpoints compromised across Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia, and other Asian nations over a 10-month campaign; long-term espionage access to government communications and sensitive policy data.

incidents.vector: Iranian state-aligned actor CL-STA-1178 delivered ShelbyLoader V2 malware via trojanized Dubai Airports coding challenges, using AppDomainManager hijacking and DLL sideloading for stealthy execution with GitHub as command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Confirmed intrusions into Iraqi critical infrastructure; novel AppDomainManager hijacking technique allowed attackers to bypass endpoint detection; GitHub C2 blended with legitimate traffic to evade network monitoring.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters used social engineering to breach Odido, the Netherlands' third-largest telecom operator.
incidents.impact: Data on 6.2 million Dutch citizens stolen — roughly one-third of the Netherlands' total population — from a major national telecommunications provider.

incidents.vector: Fraudsters used AI voice-cloning to impersonate Intesa Sanpaolo's CEO in a message to Fideuram's chairman, convincing executives to authorize large wire transfers to accounts in China and Hong Kong.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108M) stolen; Intesa Sanpaolo recovered approximately half but €36 million remains missing; perpetrators unidentified.
